meetings.title: 10th Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the committee reviewed the issue submitted stating that the government failed to provide equitable opportunities to purchase government housing units under the settlement agreement formulated between the government and the victims of the case where SeaLife Global Private Limited failed to construct housing units after collecting booking fees and down payments under the agreement signed between Housing Development Corporation and SeaLife Global Private Limited to construct 3,000 (three thousand) housing units in Hulhumalé. In this regard Ihavandhoo constituency member Ahmed Naseer proposed to share the information received from Housing Development Corporation Limited regarding the matter with the member who submitted the issue, which was seconded by Thoddoo constituency member Hussain Sameer. This proposal was passed unanimously by the members present and voting. Following that, the committee reviewed the information received from Maldives Ports Limited regarding the issue submitted concerning the challenges faced by cargo vessels transporting goods to the atolls due to the new regulation implemented by Maldives Ports Limited regarding the use of Malé North Harbor. Accordingly, Maavashu constituency member Ahmed Shakir proposed to meet with Maldives Ports Limited to further clarify information regarding the matter, which was seconded by Thoddoo constituency member Hussain Sameer. This proposal was passed by the majority of the members present and voted. Next, the committee reviewed the issue submitted regarding the public disclosure of the queue list of individuals who have made payments to register for the Hajj pilgrimage maintained by Maldives Hajj Corporation Limited. In this regard, Gadhdhoo constituency member Mohamed Ali proposed to share the information received from the corporation regarding the matter with the member who submitted the issue, which was seconded by Komandoo constituency member Mohamed Ibrahim This motion was passed unanimously by the members present and voting. Subsequently, regarding the proposal to meet with the Anti-Corruption Commission to clarify information on cases investigated by the Commission concerning state-owned enterprises and measures that can be taken to strengthen these companies, since the meeting with the Commission had already taken place and the information had been clarified, it was passed to conclude and remove the matter from the committee's status by the majority of members present and voting. Last of all, the committee unanimously passed to remove the issue regarding the matter submitted by the Maldives Marketing and Public Relations Corporation Limited (MMPRC) requesting to meet with the Committee concerning the Committee's review report on the status of MMPRC and the Maldives Integrated Tourism Development Corporation Limited (M20/R/SOE/2025/02), since the meeting was postponed at the company's request and no subsequent date was provided. Details of votes taken in this meeting are on “Votes” section of this page.

meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the committee sat with officials from State Trading Organization Public Limited, State Pharmaceutical and Medical Supply Corporation Limited, along with National Social Protection Agency and Aasandha Company Limited to discuss the issue submitted by North Galolhu Constituency member Mohamed Ibrahim to clarify misunderstandings arising in communications about procuring medicines unavailable in the Maldives from abroad. Below are the highlights of the meeting. State Trading Organization Public Limited (STO) The company’s officials have access to live medicine stock levels across pharmacies under its management. However, hospitals and doctors do not have access to this information. Not all medicines on the Food and Drug Authority’s approved list are currently available, and significant challenges are faced in the importation of medicine. The procurement of 54 types of medicine has commenced under bulk procurement, and State Pharma will continue this work moving forward. State Pharmaceutical and Medical Supply Corporation Limited Effective from 1st April 2026, a 24-hour call center has been established, and a web application (portal) has been introduced to submit requests for medicine. The company’s target is to deliver medicine to citizens within 14 (fourteen) days of the request being submitted. From 1st July 2026, the operations for importing medicine and medical consumables will be transferred under the company’s mandate. It will take 6 (six) months from the date of takeover to complete the transfer of STO pharmacies to the company, facilitate advance ordering of required medicines, and establish the entire necessary system. Furthermore, upon assuming these responsibilities, the corporation will implement a real-time inventory management system to ensure live monitoring of pharmaceutical stocks. Aasandha Company Limited Pharmacies cannot be empaneled unless they stock the medicines included in the Essential Medicine List. It is the responsibility of each pharmacy to add its available medicine stock to the registry list to provide those medicines under the Aasandha scheme. The primary challenge in providing medicine services under the Aasandha scheme is the frequent change in imported brands. To resolve this, it has been advised to use the generic names of medicines when prescribing. National Social Protection Agency (NSPA) Financial assistance continues to be provided to individuals seeking aid for the procurement of medicine.

meetings.title: 1st Meeting 2026
meetings.summary: During the meeting, the members discussed a case submitted by North Galolhu Constiuency member Mohamed Ibrahim concerning the death of an employee of State Electric Company Limited (STELCO) after an incident at the Hulhumale' Phase 1 power station. As proposed by Dhiggaru Constiuency member Amed Nazim and seconded by Maavashu Consitituency member Ahmed Shakir, the committee unanimously decided to obtain necessary information from relevant authorities before scheduling such issues proposed by the Parliament members. Therefore, the committee decided to obtain information from STELCO regarding the matter. Then, the committee discussed an issue submitted by Maavashu Consitituency member Ahmed Shakir to investigate the corruption scandal involving the purchase of gas from Maldive Gas. As proposed by Dhiggaru Constiuency member Ahmed Nazim and seconded by North Maafannu Consitituency member Mohamed Nazim, the committee unanimously decided to obtain written information from State Trading Organization (STO) and later schedule a meeting with them. Furthermore, the research report on procurement, recruitment, and the enhancement of corporate social responsibility systems in state-owned companies by the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) was discussed. As proposed by Thoddoo Constituency member Hussain Sameer and seconded by North Maafannu Consitituency member Mohamed Nazim, the committee unanimously decided to schedule this discussion after giving the members a period of 10 days to further review the report. Details of votes taken in this meeting are on “Votes” section of this page.

meetings.title: 12th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today's meeting, the Committee met with representatives from Fenaka Corporation Limited regarding the company’s Special review report submitted by PCB for the year 2022 and the current electricity issues faced by Addu City. In this regard, the management of Fenaka Corporation informed the committee that they are actively working on and implementing reforms based on the recommendations given by the Privatization and Corporatization Board. The company is currently reviewing its human resource policy, salary structure, and procurement policy, with the process expected to be completed by January 2026. In addition to that they also noted that discussions are ongoing with suppliers to install 5 generators of 6 megawatts each, with a total capacity to produce 13 megawatts of electricity to permanently solve the electricity issue in Addu City. They also mentioned that works are ongoing to produce 30 megawatts of electricity in Addu City, and the project is anticipated to be finished within one and half years. Fenaka Corporation Limited's meeting participants: Major (Retired) Mohamed Najah, Managing Director Mr. Mohamed Arif, Deputy Managing Director Ms. Kulsoom Ali, Chief Corporate Officer Mr. Fahud Mohamed, Risk and Compliance Officer

meetings.summary: In today’s committee, members discussed the issue sent by North Galolhu constituency member Mohamed Ibrahim regarding the mechanism for exchange of real-time information under the 5 th Amendment Act of Act no: 12/2016 (Criminal Procedure Code). As establishing the mechanism for exchange of real-time information is a responsibility of Maldives Monetary Authority it was decided to send the issue to Public Accounts Committee. Although it was decided in the last meeting of the committee to meet Fenaka Corporation Limited and Male' Water and Sewerage Company Private Limited, Gadhdhoo constituency member Mohamed Ali proposed to meet the officials of both the companies after the month of Ramazan and to obtain the required information in writing. Maavashu constituency member Ahmed Shakir proposed to summon the officials of both companies on 27 th February 2025. It was seconded by Thoddoo constituency member Hussain Sameer. However, since the first proposal on the issue has been passed, no vote has been taken on this proposal The voting details are on “Votes” section of this page.

meetings.title: 5th Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the committee discussed regarding the formation of sub committees. After dividing state-owned companies into eight main areas, members were appointed to these sub-committees to study the issues related to them. After that the committee discussed the issue sent by Housing Development Corporation mentioning the administrative challenges faced by the corporation due to the directives of Anti-Corruption Commission to halt works of some projects. It was decided to take the issue from the committee’s status as the company had informed the committee that the situation was no longer in place after the new government assumed office as it was a temporary measure taken during the transition process. In addition to that, members discussed the issue sent by North Galholhu member Mohamed Ibrahim to review whether the relevant authorities have carried out the works stated in the State Owned Enterprises Committee’ report no. M19/SOE/2023/01 (The issue of withdrawal of money from the accounts of Bank of Maldives customers without the knowledge of the owners of the accounts) and the challenges faced by the authorities in implementing the recommendations of the report. It was decided to meet the officials of Bank of Maldives, Maldives Monitory Authority, Maldives Police Services and Maldives Correctional Service to clarify the facts regarding the matter, as none of the members objected. Furthermore, the committee decided to obtain information regarding previous managements corruption issues and action taken by the new management to mitigate those risks from Housing Development Corporation, Waste Management Corporation, Fenaka Corporation Limited, Maldives Ports Limited, Maldives Airports Company Limited and State Electric Company Limited as none of the members objected. The committee also decided to write to Fenaka Corporation Limited about the details of the projects awarded for providing water and sewage in islands, the projects that were sub-contracted among those, the status of the work and the amount of money spent on those projects.

meetings.title: 3rd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, privatization and corporatization board was summoned to clarify the information on its annual report for 2023 and the challenges faced in the board’s functioning. In this regard the members were briefed regarding the valuable work done by the board in the past year and the challenges faced by the board in carrying out the functioning. The committee decided to write to the board to clarify the information members wanted. The committee allocated the 33 state-owned enterprises into 9 main sectors and decided to assign each sector to 9 individual sub-committees to review the issues related to those state-owned enterprises. At last, the presented committee members unanimously agreed to summon Anti-Corruption Commission to the committee to clarify the issues investigated by the commission regarding state-owned enterprises and for actions to be taken to strengthen the companies, as proposed by south Fuvahmulah constituency member Ibrahim Hussain.

meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2024
meetings.summary: The first part of today's meeting was to discuss and take a decision on the rules to be followed in the committee. According to the draft paper presented to the committee by secretariat, if the committee's legal number has not been presented the committee will be cancelled after a wait of 15 minutes from the scheduled time. An amendment to this section to change the waiting time from 15 minutes to 10 minutes was proposed by Gamu Constituency member Yoosuf Nasheed, which was seconded by Faresmaathodaa Constituency member Ashraf Rasheed. This amendment was passed by the committee as no objection was made. Subsequently, the white paper prepared by Anti-Corruption Commission to identify the visible changes in the registration system of private companies was decided to be shared to members through e-mail and to withdraw the matter out of the committee's status. Then, the committee decided to get a latest update on the matter received from Housing Development Corporation mentioning the administrative challenges faced by the corporation due to the command of Anti-Corruption Commission to halt works of some projects through the letter number 123-ES/161/2023/11 (30 th October 2023). The proposal of Dhiggaru Constituency member Ahmed Nazim to set up sub-committees to study the status of state-owned companies, seconded by Maavashu Constituency member Ahmed Shakir was passed as there was no objection from the members presented. Also, the committee decided to meet with Privatization and Corporatization Board to discuss the monitoring system of state-owned companies as proposed by North Maafannu Constituency member Mohamed Nazim, seconded by Kinbidhoo Constituency member Ali Ashrag.
